sections.md: Rome won the Second Punic War (218-201 BCE) [E] by refusing to lose a long war of attrition, even after [[Cannae|event]] (216 BCE) destroyed a Roman army [E]. Carthage won famous battles but could not break Rome's network of Italian allies [L].

block.title: After Cannae
block.because: This is what you just predicted

sections.md: Rome avoided another set-piece disaster and kept fielding armies [E]. [[Fabius|person]]'s delaying strategy denied Hannibal a decisive battle [E]. [[Scipio|person]] later took the war to Africa (204 BCE) [E], forcing Hannibal home before [[Zama|event]] (202 BCE) [E].

The first war left Carthage with an indemnity and without Sicily [E]. Rome then took Sardinia and Corsica in 238 BCE, which some historians see as opportunistic and a lasting grievance [C]. The immediate trigger was the siege of [[Saguntum|place]] by [[Hannibal|person]] in 219 BCE [E].
Carthage lost its overseas empire and effective navy [E]. Rome became the dominant power of the western Mediterranean [E], and a Third Punic War ended with the destruction of Carthage in 146 BCE [E].
